To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

– (1) conformant explanations are the natural extension of MCEs in case of model multiplicity and uncertainty, (2) the search space of MCEs is the exact same as the search space of conformant explanations with a slight modification in the equivalence criterion, (3) superfluous information can be eliminated from the explanations using the same anytime approach that is used to compute MCE, and (4) multiple explainees can be handled in the same way as model multiplicity

(1) the concept of MCEs can be generalized to the case of model multiplicity by representing the human’s mental models as annotated models; (ii) the search for conformant explanations can thus be reduced to the original MACE search; (iii) the search for such conformant explanations can also be made anytime; and (iv) the model reconciliation process can be viewed as an instance of uncertain models in the case of multiple humans in loop.

– (1) conformant explanations can help the robot explain itself with respect to multiple possible models; (2), conformant explanations can contain redundant information which can be reduced via the generation of conditional explanations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions – (1) How can the agent’s explanation generation process evolve in the presence of model uncertainty or incompletence?
how an agent can reconcile its model with that of a human’s mental model in the presence of uncertainty or incompletenes in the human model.
how the robot can explain its plans and decisions in the presence of uncertainty over the human’s mental models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work is the first to show how model reconciliation can be performed in the presence of uncertainty or multiplicity in human mental models, and how such a process can be performed in a scalable manner.
this paper shows how the explanation generation processes evolves in the presence model uncertainty and incompleteness by computing conformant explanations that apply to a set of models.
we show how the concept of model reconciliation can be generalized and extended from a setting where the model of the explainee is known precisely to one in which it is uncertain or incomplete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the model reconciliation approach can be extended to deal with uncertainty over the human’s model.

we show how the model reconciliation framework can be extended to handle uncertainty in the human’s knowledge of the problem, and how the resulting explanations can be iterated with the human to arrive at a common ground.

we are interested in the problem of model reconciliation in human-agent collaboration where the agent’s understanding of the human’s mental state is uncertain and where there are multiple humans in the collaboration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the problem of model uncertainty or incompletions may be hard to solve in the general case, the same problem can be solved efficiently by exploiting the underlying search strategy used in computing MCEs.
the model reconciliation process can be viewed as one of model uncertainty and can be addressed using the same set of techniques as those used for model uncertainty in the presence of a single human.

the model reconciliation process does not have to be an expensive process for the robot, but can be made efficient by exploiting the fact that explanations are computed with respect to the same underlying model.
